summary: Hiroshi Yamashita is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Madras. He served as an associate professor at Tohoku University (attested 1996–1999).
Hirotomo Teranishi succeeded Hiroshi Kanno in 2009. He served as director at Soka University (attested 2010–2011).

Buddhist studies scholar Hisao Inagaki studied at Ryukoku University (~1948–1953) and the University of London (~1966–1968). He held a post at SOAS University of London (1970) and was a professor at Ryukoku University (~1981–1998).
Hisao Kanaseki, who worked in Buddhist studies and other fields, studied at Doshisha University (~1939–1943). He held a post at Tokyo Metropolitan University from circa 1958 to 1982.

Hisao Takahashi is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1970–1975) under Ryukai Mano. At Taisho University, he served as an assistant (~1975–1985), lecturer (~1985–1996), and professor (~1996–2015).

Hisashi Matsumura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts at the Australian National University (attested 1982) and as an assistant professor at Kobe Shinwa University (attested 1996).

Hisashi Sato was a Tibetology and history scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1934–1937). He served as a professor at Kyoto University (~1964–1977), Komazawa University (~1977–1984), and Toyo University, and held a post at Bukkyo University (~1984–1989).

Hisataka Ishida works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna in 2011 under Helmut Krasser, Akira Saito, Hiroshi Marui, Yoichi Fukuda, and Masahiro Inami, and became a lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 2015).
Buddhist studies scholar Hitoshi Inui studied under Kanjin Horiuchi. He served at Koyasan University as a lecturer (attested 1986–1992) and later as a professor (attested 2015).

Hitoshi Katō works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and philosophy. In 1992, he held posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies, Nara University of Education, and Otani University, later becoming a professor at Osaka University (attested 2016–2017).

Hitoshi Obara, a scholar of history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies, studied at Hokkaido University (~1963–1967). He served as a professor at the University of the Sacred Heart from circa 1991 to 2015.

Hjalmar Edgren was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln and under William Dwight Whitney (~1872–1874). He held posts at Lund University (~1880–1885), the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (~1885–1901), and the University of Gothenburg (~1891–1893).
Linguist Hla Pe studied at the University of Yangon (~1931–1935) and the University of London (~1938–1944). He also taught Gustaaf Houtman.
Ho-chin Yang is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Washington in 1994, studying under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp.
Ho-sung Kim is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who founded the Institute for the History of Japanese Buddhism. He served as a professor at Dongguk University (attested 2011).

Hojun Nagasaki, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1962–1965). He served as a professor at Otani University (~1970–1999) and president of the Japanese Association for Jain Studies in 1998.

Holly Gayley is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who completed doctoral studies at Harvard University (~2001–2009). She held a post at the University of Colorado Boulder circa 2008.

Hong Luo, who works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, completed doctoral studies at Peking University. Luo has held posts at the China Tibetology Research Center and as a professor at Sichuan University.

Honsho Ueda is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer (attested 1963) and professor (attested 1992) at Minobusan Junior College, and as a professor of Buddhist studies at Minobusan University (attested 1996–2001).
Hoong Teik Toh, a scholar of sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, earned a PhD at Harvard University in 2004, having studied under Gray Tuttle, Ruohong Li, Hongmei Jin, and Yudru Tsomu.
